title: Removing Bottlenecks
summary:
Removing Bottlenecks
The main culprit behind the recent uncharacteristically deep discount of West Texas Intermediate's (WTI) price compared to Brent is the rapid rise of domestic and Canadian oil flows into Cushing, Oklahoma. Faced with costly and constricted transportation routes out of the Cushing terminal, crude oil producers rely on price discounts to make these typically light, low sulfur oils attractive. Helping to ease the cost of moving inland crude oil to US Gulf Coast markets is the flow reversal of the Seaway pipeline that is scheduled for completion this coming May.
